fields.prompt: [1] (SATA) In which of the following locations exist temperature inversions?
[1] (MCQ) Which of the following layers of the atmosphere has the highest temperature?
[1] (MCQ) Which of the following boundaries define the “edge” of the atmosphere?
[1] (MCQ) According to Earth’s energy budget, how much energy is absorbed by land and oceans?
[1] (MCQ) Which of the following does NOT determine how much insolation is received at a surface?
[1] (MCQ) Wet soil changes temperature at a slower rate than dry soil. This means wet soil has a ___ average heat capacity than dry soil.

[2] (FRQ) On a very cold day, a puddle of water gradually cools to ice just before you stick a thermometer in it. You observe that the puddle was at 0 degrees Celsius before and after it froze and also observe an increase in the temperature of the air above the puddle. Explain this increase in temperature and what type of heat caused it.
fields.answer: Liquid water and ice can both exist at 0 C. For liquid water to turn into ice, the intermolecular bonds must form and strengthen to become ice, a process that releases heat. This heat is not associated with a temperature change of the water and is called latent heat.

criteria.answer: Intermolecular bonds form and release heat during phase change
Heat is latent heat not associated with temperature change

[1] (MCQ) Which of the following cloud types would you expect to “trap” the most solar radiation?

[4] (FRQ) The air temperature is generally above the dew point. As expected, as the air temperature decreases towards the dew point, the relative humidity increases. However, the amount of water vapor in the air can stay the same during this process. Why is this possible? In other words, why would the relative humidity increase as temperature decreases even though the water vapor content remains the same?
fields.answer: A decrease in temperature decreases the amount of water vapor that the air can hold, and relative humidity is defined as the amount of water vapor in the air out of the amount it can hold. Thus, even though the amount of water vapor stays the same, the amount that can be held decreases, increasing relative humidity.

criteria.answer: Decrease in temperature decreases the water vapor capacity
accepted: temperature decreases the amount of water vapor that the air can hold

criteria.answer: Relative humidity is ratio of water vapor to capacity
accepted: relative humidity is defined as the amount of water vapor in the air out of the amount it can hold

fields.prompt: [3] (FRQ) We know that temperature decreases as altitude increases in the troposphere. Therefore, the relative humidity of a rising parcel of air in the troposphere will keep increasing in relative humidity until its water vapor condenses. What is the name of the altitude at which this condensation first occurs?
[2] (FRQ) The previous question assumes that the air parcel is rising. Identify and explain two reasons an air parcel might lift.
fields.answer: Any two of the following: Orographic lift, convergent lift, convective lift, frontal lift.

fields.prompt: [4] (FRQ) Calculate the average pressure gradient (SI units) from South Dakota to North Wisconsin. Assume the distance is roughly 700 miles. Show your work.
fields.answer: 3.1e-3 Pa/m. The pressure over SD is 1031 mb = 103100 Pa and Wisconsin is 996 mb = 99600 Pa. The pressure difference is 3500 Pa. The distance, in meters, is 700 miles * 1609 meters/mile = 1126300 meters. Pressure gradient = 3500 / 1126300 = 3.1e-3 Pa/m.

criteria.answer: Pressure over SD and WI identified correctly

fields.context: Refer to the surface weather map shown in image 4 for questions 47 - 52

fields.prompt: [2] (FRQ) It is evident that the actual pressure gradient from the previous question is not uniform. In other words, you calculated the average pressure gradient. Where (closer to SD or WI) would you expect a steeper gradient? Explain.
fields.answer: Closer to WI. Isobars are much more tightly packed near the low pressure cell, so pressure is changing more rapidly with distance, causing a steeper pressure gradient.

criteria.answer: Isobars are tightly packed near low pressure
accepted: isobars are much more tightly packed
